source.title: On the Computational Entanglement of Distant Features in Adversarial Machine Learning
source.authors: Yen-Lung Lai; Xing-Bo Dong; Zhe Jin; Anhui Provincial

record.file_problem: Full text is present. It includes figure captions and descriptions, but the figures themselves are not available for reading precise plotted values.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports experiments on unseen random inputs, but they do not test the listed versions’ natural-label test error, training recipes, or measured gap properties. The authors say whether the observed behavior benefits generalization remains open.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on memorization and generalization, but those cited results are not rows. Its own unseen-input loss results are recorded under fits_no_version because the experiments do not measure training-versus-test error on natural labels.
record.test_reason: The study measures alignment and normalized distance between outputs of toy linear networks on synthetic inputs. It does not measure any listed version's classification performance, optimizer or batch-size comparison, dropout benefit, sharpness–gap relationship, or example-removal effect. Its zero-loss claims concern a different construct from fitting fixed random labels and generalizing on natural labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report computational entanglement in overparameterized linear networks, demonstrate related collapse with gradient descent, and apply it to information reconciliation and image recovery. They explicitly leave its benefit for generalization unresolved and do not claim that non-robust features improve generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses unsupervised maximum-likelihood optimization of linear networks and a toy gradient-descent distance-minimization experiment; neither evaluates standard natural-label training and test error.
record.method_sensitivity: The text says loss collapse is associated with larger L and n in the MaxLikelihood experiment, and with increasing λ or a larger learning rate η in the gradient-descent experiment; exact figure values are unavailable.

fits_no_version.finding: After MaxLikelihood optimization on one input, normalized outputs for unseen Gaussian inputs approach correlation or anti-correlation with the training output as depth and candidate width increase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A norm-maximizing procedure in linear networks can produce collapse of output directions on unseen synthetic inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: In the toy gradient-descent experiment, normalized output-distance loss approaches zero or one as target scale increases; the text reports similar behavior with a larger learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing target scale or learning rate can induce output-alignment collapse in a toy linear distance-minimization task.

record.problems: The results are for feedforward linear toy networks and synthetic random inputs, not natural-label classification. Precise values and settings are presented only in figures unavailable in the supplied text. The gradient-descent section says whether the minimum solution benefits generalization remains open.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results were left out. Cited prior-work results were excluded because the study does not report them as its own.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under matched architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes that recover held-out performance.
Effects of dropout, training-set size, augmentation, and joint dropout–weight-decay removal on held-out error. Algorithm 1's row-selection step, called dropout, supplies no such comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its relationship to generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports the qualitative collapse descriptions despite unavailable plotted values. Neither these descriptions nor the information-reconciliation and image-recovery demonstrations supply results on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random labels with held-out performance on natural labels using the same architecture and recipe.
Does not sweep width against natural-label test error or identify an interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on image classification.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out benchmark performance.
Does not compare batch sizes or their effects on held-out performance.
Does not test dropout or weight decay effects on held-out error.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or relate it to a training-test gap.
Does not remove memorized training examples or measure the resulting test accuracy.

rows.value: Figure only; text says loss values collapse toward zero or one, and large enough n and L yield zero loss.
rows.note: The outcome is a computed angular loss on unseen random inputs, not test error on natural labels or a measured training-test gap.
rows.check: The angular alignment loss cannot establish any listed version. Section III uses input length l = 2 as its example and 5,000 Gaussian test samples. The text reports collapse toward both zero and one; zero loss must not be presented as applying uniformly to all unseen samples. The qualitative result is stated in the text, so evidence_form should not be figure_only.

new, random, previously unseen inputs in R2

rows.measure: Computed normalized L2 loss on unseen inputs
rows.value: Figure only; text says loss collapses to zero or one as λ increases.
rows.note: This is a toy distance-minimization task, not standard training on natural labels or a training-test error comparison.
rows.check: Normalized output distance does not establish any listed version. Section V describes G* = G3G2G1 with L = 3, but Algorithm 2 directly updates a single 2×2 matrix G*; the implementation description is inconsistent. Algorithm 2 specifies w0 = [0.1, 0.1] and target λ[1, 1]. T = 5 is an illustrative iteration count, not an established setting for every plotted result. Loss collapse is also reported textually.
